page.layout: One page of text in two columns of running text, the left column wider than the right; no margin notes beyond the marginal reference letters in the left margin. Running head at the top right. Page number at the top right. Line-ending letters in the left margin are fragments of text on the facing page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: Inter alia ridicula ac fuperftitiofa quæ à Pontifi-ciis mutuatur, hæc funt. Nam 1. Presbyteri tenentur matutinas & vespertinas illas preces fingulis diebus publice vel privatim prælegere, pag. libri illius. 7. Porro si privatim & folus prælegat, quis ufus refponfionum per populum: nisi forte intelligendum sit, debere presbyterum sibi respondere nomine ecclesiæ quam repræfentat, & sic preces hæ cum sint publica authoritate institutæ, & prolatæ à publica persona, deputata ab ecclesia ad orandum nomine suo, & hac intentione ut expleat munus suum, quid aliud erunt quam preces illæ Papistarum publicæ, seu horæ Canonicæ, quarum duæ ex septem reponuntur. vide Bellarm. tom. 4. Controvers. lib. 1. De bonis operibus in particulari. cap. 10. 2. Nullus certus locus destinatur matutinis & vespertinis precibus publicis; sed remittitur arbitrio Episcopi, qui sedulo studebit templorum formam ad tempora præcedentia revocare, hoc est, quando Papismus regnabat, ad similitudinem fcil. templi Salomonis, divisi in porticum, navim, & sacrarium. 3. Quædam alta voce à presbytero proferenda sunt, alia vero voce submissa, quæ forma pontificiis confueta est in mysterio Missæ, preces etiam quædam, confessio fidei, & alia jubentur legi aut cani, cum tamen in metrum non redigantur. 4. licet situs corporis indifferens sit, in quibusdam tamen precibus indicitur, ut genibus flexis precemur; in aliis ut stemus; in aliis vero nullus omnino corporis situs imperatur; Et aliquando populus jubetur orare non presbyter, & vice versa, aliquando populus jubetur comprecari cum presbytero, quandoque repetit, quandoque respondet, & alias orationem inter se dividunt, jubetur presbyter aliquando faciem ad populum convertere, aliquando ergo avertit: stare cum

page.notes: Marginal letters and fragments of the facing page at the left edge are not transcribed. Several words in the lower lines are slightly blurred; the final line ("cum") is a catchword-like continuation and is kept in the text. Printed text is in Latin with some long-s forms rendered as s; the fragment "s" was normalised. Some words in the text are doubtful and not individually marked.
